verdict_reason: The added doc line is placed correctly but implies the JS results route saves nothing, when it commits the stored search rows on every refresh just as the full-page search post does.

todos.issue: architecture.md:169-170 says the results route 'renders only the results and saves no lines', which reads as a side-effect-free route. It is not: postResults (search.controller.js:228) runs showSelectionWork -> searchAndStoreRows -> replaceStoredSearchRows (selection/rows.js:35-38), which state.commit()s the stored search rows on every refresh, exactly as the no-JS search post does. Neither post saves commodity lines (only commitSelection on Continue does), so 'saves no lines' draws a contrast with the full-page post that does not exist and hides the write the route does make.
todos.fix: Must: the bullet says what the results route saves and what it does not, in the same terms as the full-page post, so a reader does not take it for a read-only route. One way: 'With JavaScript the same post goes to the page's results route, which saves the search rows as the full-page post does but renders only the results.'
